<head>
  <meta charset="UTF-8">
  <meta name="viewport" content="width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0">
  <title>ae683f770</title>
  <style>
    *, *::before, *::after {
      box-sizing: border-box;
      margin: 0;
      padding: 0;
    }
    html, body {
      height: 100%;
    }
    body {
      min-height: 100vh;
      min-height: 100dvh;
      display: grid;
      place-items: center;
      overflow: hidden;
    }
    svg {
      display: block;
      width: min(400px, 90vmin);
      height: auto;
      aspect-ratio: 1;
    }
    circle {
      fill: currentColor;
    }
  </style>
</head>
<body>
  <svg id="ae683f770" viewBox="0 0 400 400" role="img" aria-labelledby="ae683f770-title">
    <title id="ae683f770-title">Circle</title>
    <circle cx="200" cy="200" r="200"/>
  </svg>
</body>
</html>

I updated `0.html`. It still shows the same black circle; the changes are all under the hood. I haven't opened it in a browser to check.

- **No more scrollbars:** the old `100vw`/`100vh` sizing could create scrollbars on some browsers. The page now uses `100%` height and `dvh` units (which fit mobile screens properly), and centers the circle with a grid.
- **Scales on small screens:** the SVG is now `min(400px, 90vmin)`, so it shrinks to fit phones instead of spilling off the edge.
- **Cleaner CSS:** the reset now includes `box-sizing: border-box`, and the SVG is set to `display: block` so there's no stray gap underneath it.
- **Accessibility:** screen readers now read the graphic as an image called "Circle".
- **Color:** the circle takes its color from the surrounding text color, so you can theme it with one `color` setting.

If you meant something else by "improve", like a visual redesign or animation, tell me what you have in mind.
